slides.head:
Musk promised a full AI Odyssey.
Grok shipped seven minutes.
Seven minutes, not a film.
slides.body: On October 23 the Grok Imagine account posted Episode 1 of an AI Odyssey series on X: seven minutes made with Grok Imagine, in collaboration with AI studio Wonder Studios and director Dev Walker.

slides.head: The promise was a feature.
slides.body: In July, Elon Musk said Grok would make a full-length, historically accurate movie of The Odyssey before the end of 2026. Three months later, this is the first chapter. The post offered a breakdown of how it was made to anyone who asked.

slides.head:
Photoreal, until
Penelope changed.
slides.body: Some viewers praised the photorealism. Others pointed to Penelope looking different in each scene, flat voices and glassy eyes. The Telegraph called the effect zombie-like. TechCrunch found no momentum and no reason to care.

slides.head: $1.78 billion, mostly practical.
slides.body: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, shot across six countries with a cast and crew of thousands and built mainly on practical filmmaking, opened in July and has grossed more than $1.78 billion worldwide.

slides.head:
Shots are cheap.
Scenes are not.
slides.body: The footage held up one shot at a time. It fell apart the moment it had to carry a character across two scenes. Continuity, performance and a reason to care are still the work. Generate the shots. Direct the story.
